titleStmt.title: Mr. Munenori to Mr. Von Eisendecher.

opener.seg: [Inclosure 1 in No. 935.—Extract from the Japan Daily Herald, August 7, 1879.—Translation.]

head.hi: Mr. Munenori to Mr. Von Eisendecher.

opener.dateline:
Foreign Office, Tokei,
The 31st, the 7th month, the 12th year Meiji.

div.p: Sir: I have the honor to acknowledge the receipt of your excellency’s letter, dated 21st instant, relative to the detention of steamship Hesperia, in which you give the motives for your manner of proceeding with that vessel, by contending that the quarantine regulations promulgated by the Japanese Government are not obligatory for German subjects and vessels, unless they are sanctioned by the German consular authority.

In reply, I beg to state that the position taken by your excellency, as above stated, bas never been and cannot be admitted by this government, as it is, in my opinion, directly in opposition to international law and the existing treaty stipulations.

Your excellency is, no doubt, aware that according to well-known principles of international law even the persons who are entitled to the privilege of exterritoriality are bound to observe the police regulations of the country where they reside, and that by the existing treaty, if a certain portion of jurisdiction is conceded to the German consular authorities, it does not follow that they are entitled to claim participation in the proper administration of the government.

Notwithstanding the explanation you furnished in the note of 21st, I regret to find that your excellency has been led to a proceeding which appears to me to have been executed with unnecessary haste and without any just reason, and against which I consider it my duty to formally protest.
I avail myself of this occasion to renew to your excellency the assurance of my highest consideration.

closer.signed:
TERASHIMA MUNENORI,
His Imperial Japanese Majesty’s Minister for Foreign Affairs.
